The story does not provide diverse perspectives, nor does it delve into the mindset of morally ambiguous, objectionable, or repugnant characters. It is written strictly from a limited third-person perspective focused entirely on a single character, Ilse. While her son Jonas represents a different lifestyle (coming from Munich to the rural Elbe), the narrative never enters his viewpoint or explores his internal motivations; the reader only observes him through Ilse's eyes. Furthermore, neither character is depicted as particularly unlikeable or morally objectionable—Ilse is simply stoic and guarded, and the story focuses on a quiet, tender moment of familial reconnection rather than challenging the reader with difficult or repugnant worldviews.
